units.note: The DefaultInstanceBrowseName Property exists only as a node of the standard NodeSet; nothing serves it on an ObjectType and no test reads one.
The HasAddIn ReferenceType is imported with the standard NodeSet; no server code or test uses it.

Every Variable serves AccessLevelEx (Part 3 §8.58). NonatomicRead and NonatomicWrite are 0 for a Value the server stores, which a Read gets and a Write replaces whole under the lock of the Node; an application sets them on a Variable whose ValueFunc or ValueWriter cannot ensure atomicity (SetAttribute of AccessLevelEx).

Every NodeClass with its Attributes and References is served and tested. A Variable that stores no AccessLevel, UserAccessLevel or Historizing (NewVariableNode, imported Variables without Historizing) reads them with the values the server applies (Part 3 §5.6.2), as do the Variables of a MapNamespace.

A Variable whose AccessLevelEx sets WriteFullArrayOnly refuses a Write with an IndexRange with Bad_WriteNotSupported (Part 3 §8.58, Part 4 §5.11.4.2); without it the IndexRange is merged. The application sets the bit with SetAttribute of AccessLevelEx.

InterfaceTypes, BaseInterfaceType and HasInterface come from the standard NodeSet and imported HasInterface References are browsable; the rules of Interfaces on instances are neither applied nor tested.
The NonVolatile and Constant bits of AccessLevelEx are never set; no test.
Read of several Attributes of several Nodes, with IndexRange on arrays, ByteStrings and matrices.
An IndexRange Write merges into arrays, ByteStrings and matrices, with the refusals asserted; no ledger row writes with an IndexRange.
Only a Variable with an application ValueWriter receives a written StatusCode or timestamp; for a value the server stores it answers Bad_WriteNotSupported, which the ledger rows verify.
Batch Writes of Values and of the Attributes the WriteMask allows, with a status per operation.

Root, Objects, the Server Object, NamespaceArray, ServerStatus, Auditing, VendorServerInfo and ServerRedundancy are served; ServerArray is the ApplicationUri, ServiceLevel follows the ServerState in the sub-ranges of Part 4 §6.6.2.4.2 and RedundancySupport is None (Part 5 §6.3.1, §6.3.7). No ledger row reads ServerArray or ServiceLevel.
The Views Object is imported with the standard NodeSet and asserted; the server has no View of its own.
No CurrencyUnit Property support; no test.

An application can add an EngineeringUnits Property by hand; no helper and no test serves one.

The SemanticsChanged bit is set after a Property with the SemanticChange AccessLevel changes by a Write or Node.SetAttribute; a change by a SetValueFunc or another data source is not seen (LIMITATIONS.md).

ServerProfileArray, LocaleIdArray, MinSupportedSampleRate, MaxBrowseContinuationPoints, MaxSessions and the five OperationLimits are served; MaxArrayLength is ua.MaxVariantArrayLength, MaxStringLength and MaxByteStringLength the largest request message (an upper bound: the server refuses a larger message and imposes no other limit), and the ModellingRules Folder organizes the five ModellingRules (Part 5 §6.3.2).
MaxMonitoredItemsQueueSize is the largest QueueSize a data MonitoredItem is granted: 100, or the MaxQueueSize of a durable Subscription (10000 by default) when larger.

MaxSubscriptions, MaxSubscriptionsPerSession, MaxMonitoredItems, MaxMonitoredItemsPerSubscription and MaxMonitoredItemsPerCall are served and tested; the AggregateFunctions Folder organizes every Aggregate an AggregateFilter calculates.
No ValueAsText Property is maintained for enumerated Variables; no test.
returnDiagnostics gives service and operation DiagnosticInfos with a string table; a Publish answered after waiting carries none (docs/server-guide.md).
FindServers returns the server's own ApplicationDescription.
The Endpoints are returned, filtered by EndpointUrl and by the Transport Profiles of profileUris, none when none matches (Part 4 §5.5.4); no ledger row sends profileUris.

docs/server-guide.md lists the SecureChannels (not limited by the server), Sessions, continuation points, Subscriptions, Publish requests, MonitoredItems, the retransmission queue and the queues of sampled and event MonitoredItems, with their defaults and options.

CreateSession, ActivateSession and CloseSession with their parameters.
ActivateSession with another user changes the identity of the Session; a refused one keeps it. No ledger row.

The authentication token is checked; every response and ServiceFault carries the requestHandle of its request (Part 4 §7.33), but for a request that cannot be decoded; a queued Publish request whose timeoutHint elapsed is answered Bad_Timeout and the next one is used (Part 4 §7.32), and a Write a ValueWriter takes ends with its timeoutHint. Other services run to completion, which §7.32 allows.

Many Sessions at once (100 by default), but one dispatcher serves the requests of all of them in turn (server/server.go): a slow Method or value function holds up every Session; only ValueWriter Writes and waiting Publish requests leave it.
CreateSubscription, ModifySubscription, DeleteSubscriptions, Publish, Republish and SetPublishingMode.
A Session queues max(100, MaxSubscriptionsPerSession+1) Publish requests.
With the queue full the oldest Publish request is answered with Bad_TooManyPublishRequests.
No option sets an acceptable clock skew.

Time Sync – OS based support is the mechanism, which docs/server-guide.md names: the server's time is the clock of the operating system, which the host synchronizes (NTP or PTP of the operating system).
Not implemented.
Not implemented; TSN is out of scope (LIMITATIONS.md).
The library has no NTP client; NTP of the operating system is Time Sync – OS based support.
Every timestamp of the server is time.Now, the clock of the operating system, which the server never sets; the host synchronizes it.
Not implemented.
